newsitem.title: UK: Norwich Union to confirm flotation - Independent.
newsitem.headline: Norwich Union to confirm flotation - Independent.

text.p: Norwich Union, Britain's second biggest mutual insurance company, will confirm this week that it plans a stock market flotation by the summer of 1997, the Independent on Sunday said. The float will capitalise the company at about 4.0 billion stg and bring an average of 500 stg or more for its three million life policy owners, the Independent said.
Norwich first needs the approval from its policy owners, who currently own the business.
Norwich will be restructured in order to free a surplus of about one billion stg that is currently locked in the life fund.
This will form the basis for the distribution to life policy holders, the paper said. The windfall will be paid out in the form of new shares.
As part of the restructuring, Norwich will raise up to 1.5 billion stg of new money from the stock market, which will be used to capitalise the life fund, the paper said.
